findings.message: hoursVisibleTo now uses Time's seesWeek, but it works out each week's project set again, and differently. It only counts entries whose day is inside the report range (`e.day between from and to`). Time's own reads (contracts.ts `weekProjects`, team.ts) count every live entry of the week. So when a week crosses the range boundary, a PM's visibility differs between Time and Reports. Fix: build the project list per week_id over the whole week, the same way as `weekProjects` (or share one helper), instead of only the entries in range.
findings.scenario: Report range 2026-10-01..2026-10-31. Kasun's week 2026-W40 (Sep 28 to Oct 2) has Fleet Tracker hours on Sep 29 and Contoso hours on Oct 1. Nimal (PM of Fleet Tracker) sees all of W40 in Time's weekTotals and Team time. The utilisation report hides Kasun's Oct 1 hours from Nimal because `projectsIn` for W40 only holds CON.

findings.message: The fix changed the 071 rule refusals and guardLock to ToolError('invalid_input'), but other Time rule refusals on the same write paths are still plain `Error`, and `userFacing()` rejects them: `guardFixable` (entry.ts:45-46, the same submitted/approved text guardLock now throws as ToolError), `guardDayTotal` (guards.ts:43), the weekend and real-date check in `workDay` (guards.ts:16-17), and requestChange's status and open-request refusals (request.ts:40, 42). Fix: throw ToolError(..., 'invalid_input') in each, and add them to the userFacing test table.
findings.scenario: REST correct_time_entry on an entry in a submitted week → guardFixable throws a plain Error → rest.ts returns 500 'internal' with a reference and hides 'is submitted and waiting for approval…'. log_time with hours that push the day past 24 h → the same 500.

findings.message: The migration says the commit_draft key is 'race-safe' (one draft per person and commit). ingest-ac2.test.ts only replays pushes one after another. No test runs two ingests of the same commit at the same time, for example a GitHub and an Azure DevOps delivery in parallel through Promise.all on separate sessions, and then checks for exactly one draft and one activity line. Fix: add that concurrent case.
findings.scenario: Two webhook deliveries of commit b2c0ffee2 arrive at the same time. Nothing in the suite shows that exactly one `delivery.commit_time` event and one 'drafted' activity line come out.

findings.message: The README still describes `hoursVisibleTo` as returning whose hours a viewer sees, with 'a PM for people with hours on a project they manage'. The contract now returns a per-(user, day) predicate scoped week by week through seesWeek, and the PM path covers only weeks with hours on a project they approve. Update the README entry for the changed contract signature and rule.

The round-1 fix switched the 071 entry-rule refusals and guardLock to ToolError, but left the other input refusals on the same write paths as plain Error. These are the weekend and not-a-real-date guards (guards.ts:16-17) and the 24 h day total in guardDayTotal (guards.ts:43). The same goes for the submitted/approved week refusals in entry.ts:45-46, and for the week-status and open-request refusals in request.ts:40,42. userFacing() (packages/mcp/src/registry.ts:23) rejects them, so REST and other reporters still return a 500 'internal' error and hide the message. This is the class the previous finding named ('wherever a rule refuses'); only the 071 instances were changed. Fix: throw ToolError(..., 'invalid_input') for every caller-input refusal in these guards, and extend the userFacing table in settings.test.ts to cover a weekend day, a day over 24 h and a submitted-week request.
findings.scenario: REST log_time {projectKey:'FLT', day:'2026-10-31', hours:1} (a Saturday) -> 500 internal with a reference, instead of a 400 saying it is a weekend. The same happens for hours that push a day past 24 h.
